Author: mithro_
Content: So, the device sucks the backing tape down onto it and then the pushers push up? Do you have control over the different push pins, or do they all go up at the same time? I assume the other things next to it are the UV leds?

Author: anfroholic
Content:
Yep, the tape is sucked down with a vacuum just like the previous version and modeled after the commercial machine i found a while back. 
No, all the pins go up at once, that's why we were asking about packing in the lower left corner. Now that i have played ( a lot ) could probably feel comfortable designing something with more fidelity, but would probably no longer use steppers. Or at least steppers as the driver. 
Yep, those are uv leds. 365nm. There isn't any extra space so 2 were needed and one will have to be used depending on the quadrant.

Author: namibj
Content:
Steppers driving what?

FYI, something like https://odriverobotics.com/ can upgrade from the 2-phase NEMA steppers to 3-phase BLDCs w/ encoders doing closed loop field oriented control. Though it _probably_ shouldn't be an issue anyways.

Author: anfroholic
Content:
The stepper drives a screw that pushes up the pins. The pusher part is just an insert that slides down inside. 
Given the timeframe, I have to choose what is most likely to work, even though you can see it still took a number of revisions (I don't even think that was all)
In the end, the number of pins had to be reduced (kept getting 'bed of nails' effect) and the vacuum needed to be embedded in the tip with some internal chambers as I was having a hard time getting seals any other way. 
As I've understood the design requirements more, I think I would try for some voice coil/solenoid options for the pins and that would allow for smaller space and fidelity on the for pin selection? That's the idea, but need to move to other areas now. 

*re: *odrive, I don't think it's not really necessary for what we have at the moment as simplicity is desired.

Author: namibj
Content:
If you think there's practical potential to modify this very design a little and add load cells into the structural backing of those pins (ideally individually) wired out to something that could eventually record and collate to what the machine was tasked with to mostly-passively gather information about the forces actually involved in the pushing work.....

While ofc not matching individual linear motor actuation of any particular variety (there's a reason "limited slip" differentials are a thing for 4WD cars....), it'd still give understanding of the forces involved and thus what nuanced actuation in the future would need force-wise/power-wise.

Author: namibj

well, the operating principle of odrive can give you a lot of speed for the seek while letting you control the deceleration good enough to keep the mechanics from ringing (much) and then still using the encoder resolution to do the fine positioning.

Though ofc regenerative braking doesn't matter as much for this as it does for a battery powered robot.

Author: namibj
Content: for these pins I'd probably have aimed at solenoid style with a non-ferromagnetic ideally not aluminium levels of electrically conductive front (maybe non-magnetic stainless steel should work great?), and a solid soft iron or at most ferrosilicon (transformer sheet alloy) active chunk; then a coil in similar encasing that sucks the pin forwards and if needed a separate one to pull them back town again.

Author: namibj
Content:
a non-magnetic tube should give easy winding mandrel and later inner solid holder for the windings that would be done.

But without knowing forces it's not at all easy to check if it'll reasonably behave if made a particular way.

Author: namibj
Content:
(I think there'd ideally be a magnetic tube of similar cross section or slightly above compared to the inner rod's magnetic iron part, around the outside of the windings, acting as shielding and to channel the magnetic field where it's wanted.
But switched reluctance motors like those technically would be are vulnerable to kinda-non-intuitive design-effects/behaviors, hence kinda preferring to sim. Thankfully the almost trivial geometry involved would make this part of the design almost trivial to pull off.)
